channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Trump, Putin and Xi at one table, without Ukraine. What Moscow wants from the proposal and why Beijing might agree.
item.description: Moscow is pushing for a summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, without Kyiv or the EU. What does Russia hope to gain, and why might China be willing to take part?

item.title: [DW] Raids at far-right group's offices at European Parliament
item.description: Authorities searched the Patriots for Europe's European Parliament offices in a long-running funding inquiry. The group says the charges pertain to its predecessor and there is "no legal continuity" between the two.

item.title: [DW] Russia arrests German man, calls him a Ukraine 'mercenary'
item.description: Russian FSB agents have arrested a German national and accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine's military. They claim he deserted over unpaid wages and say he was a sniper who once served in the Bundeswehr.

item.title: [DW] Russia frees jailed American Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff talks
item.description: During talks between Vladimir Putin and Steve Witkoff, Putin announced that jailed American Stephen Hubbard had been released. The Kremlin also said Russia was "in principle" ready to resume trilateral talks next month.

item.title: [DW] New EU plan for Arctic warily eyes influence of Russia, US
item.description: The EU unveiled its priorities in the Arctic as it vies with Russia, China and the US for influence. EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas said drone incursions, GPS jamming and cable sabotage undermine Arctic security.

item.title: [DW] Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
item.description: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU’s Arctic oil-and-gas pledge leaves a Norway-sized loophole
item.description: If there is no offtake market in continental Europe, no-ne is going to take the risk. The thing is, EU buyers already buy plenty of gas (and oil) from the Arctic.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU Parliament defies frugal capitals by seeking €7bn more for the EU’s popular Erasmus+ student scheme
item.description: The parliament overwhelmingly supported an increased budget and scope for the Erasmus+ programme under the new EU budget on Thursday.

item.title: [DW] Are the French police the most violent in the EU?
item.description: As protests continue in France, the French police are under scrutiny after new allegations of police brutality. The force has a bigger arsenal than most in Europe.

item.title: [EU Observer] Drones buzz overhead and enemy wi-fi everywhere: Ukrainian veterans describe how they survived in Russia’s ‘kill zone’ (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,701)
item.description: The kill zone’s constant drone buzz, mined roads and invisible Russian networks are making basic things, such as a phone call, into life-or-death gambles for exhausted Ukrainian troops.

item.title: [EU Observer] A bigger EU border force Frontex is set to be unveiled with emphasis on deportations
item.description: The EU's border force Frontex is getting overhauled next Tuesday by a European Commission determined to give the Warsaw-based agency a larger role in deportations, more resources, and more agility to deploy.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Life near the front line in Sloviansk
item.description: As Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, thousands of residents refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out. For many, poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation painfully difficult.

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria: Concerns about security in the Black Sea dominate presidential election campaign
item.description: Bulgaria's presidential election campaign has been shaped by recent drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea and the government's reduced support for Ukraine, making foreign policy a key factor in the first round.

item.title: [Financial Times] Why 17 is not the magic number in industrial policy
item.description: A lack of focus threatens to hobble Japanese premier Sanae Takaichi’s growth strategy

item.title: [Financial Times] SoftBank-backed drone maker wants every farmer to ‘have their own robot’
item.description: Chinese start-up XAG believes pilotless crop sprayers are the answer to a dwindling workforce and rising temperatures

item.title: [Financial Times] Co-operate to avoid being hostage to geopolitics, Australia tells ‘middle powers’
item.description: Jim Chalmers argues economic security and bolstering supply chains would benefit consumers

item.title: [Financial Times] Hundreds of thousands protest in France in second weekend of mass demonstrations
item.description: Government puts 70,000 police officers on the streets to boost security after last weekend’s riots

item.title: [Euractiv] UK, France stage mock airborne assault in Germany
item.description: It marks one of Britain’s largest airborne operations in a generation

item.title: [Financial Times] Ukraine military says Starlink service restrictions have been lifted
item.description: Slowdown in drone communication system had hampered Kyiv’s ability to defend itself against Russian strikes

item.title: [Euractiv] Milan braces for protests as police flood streets
item.description: Shopkeepers boarded up windows as thousands of demonstrators took to the streets

item.title: [Euractiv] National Rally closes ranks around re-elected leader Jordan Bardella
item.description: RN activists sought to keep controversy outside their Orléans congress

item.title: [DW] Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
item.description: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

item.title: [Euractiv] 250,000 rally in Madrid demanding state pension guarantees
item.description: Rally comes amid political row over sustainability of Spain's pension scheme and cost of living

item.title: [Politico Europe] Tensions flare up across France as marches come to an end
item.description: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez told police forces to be "uncompromising" with potential rioters.

item.title: [Euractiv] Police fire tear gas as new French demonstrations kick off
item.description: Authorities deploy 70,000 security personnel amid fears of renewed violence

item.title: [Politico Europe] Starlink connection restored at high speed in Ukraine, defense minister says
item.description: SpaceX's satellite internet service had been restricted since last week.

item.title: [Euractiv] Commission remains on alert after PHP cybersecurity flaws
item.description: The EU executive kept its websites online, unlike several European governments

item.title: [EU Observer] Calls mount for UN World Food Programme, which feeds over a million people in Gaza, to quit contract with Palantir
item.description: The UN food agency helping Palestinians and others in need across the world has come under scrutiny for its contract with Palantir –  the controversial US tech and AI company used by various international border police and militaries to sort data and better identify targets.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Bulgaria’s presidential election becomes a test of Rumen Radev’s grip on power
item.description: Bulgaria holds its presidential election on Sunday. A moment to decide whether to consolidate power around the current prime minister - prioritising stability over institutional balance.

item.title: [DW] France: Clashes break out as protests go nationwide
item.description: Police and elite security forces were out in force in French cities as tens of thousands participated in protests on Saturday. The situation turned tense toward the end of protests in several cities, including Paris.

item.title: [Financial Times] France is looking ungovernable. And it’s going to get worse
item.description: As disorder engulfs Paris and Marine Le Pen waits in the wings, the country is running out of money, patience and answers

item.title: [Financial Times] Tucker Carlson: ‘I so overstated my power it was embarrassing’
item.description: Does Trump’s loudest critic still have his finger on America’s pulse?

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ein Spaziergang mit Martin Blessing
item.description: Ist Deutschland wirklich der kranke Mann Europas oder steht ein wirtschaftliches Comeback bevor? Nach einem milliardenschweren Investitionsgipfel „Invest in Germany“ mit Tech-Größen wie Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang zieht Martin Blessing, der persönliche Beauftragte des Bundeskanzlers für Investitionen, eine optimistische Bilanz. Es bleibt die entscheidende Frage, wie viel von den zugesagten Milliarden tatsächlich frisches Geld ist und […]

item.title: [Euractiv] Two Balkan elections, one Russia dilemma
item.description: In both countries, Russia’s shadow could shape the political landscape well beyond Sunday’s vote

item.title: [Euractiv] War, huh! Are Eurobonds all it’s good for?
item.description: The EU will likely issue more common debt to finance Ukraine. Why won’t it do it for itself?

item.title: [Politico Europe] Inside the cyber flaw scramble that brought the AI threat to life
item.description: Vulnerabilities in a programming language underpinning much of the web set off a hectic 72-hour rush among virtually every cybersecurity agency in the world.

item.title: [Politico Europe] What’s not on the ballot in Israel: Peace
item.description: At some point, Israelis will have to have conversations about peace and how to reach a settlement with Palestinians. But in this election, the critical issue has just been avoided.

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
item.description: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU and China weigh next sectors for trade curbs
item.description: Trade chief Maroš Šefčovič tells POLITICO that Brussels and Beijing will review their recent trade understanding in January as they discuss which sectors to tackle next.

item.title: [DW] Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
item.description: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

item.title: [Euractiv] Hungary marks 1956 uprising amid high-profile absences
item.description: EU leaders attended Budapest commemorations, but Macron, Merz and Zelenskyy stayed away

item.title: [Euractiv] Editors’ Choice: Costa’s salt in the soup of politics
item.description: The Friday edition of our PM newsletter looks at the week that was in European politics and policy

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Ousting Netanyahu won’t curb right-wing Israeli nationalism, says expert ahead of Tuesday’s Knesset elections
item.description: Beth Oppenheim, fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, explains how a shift in Israeli society will shape voting on 27 October. Her analysis groups Israeli political forces into liberal Zionists, nationalists, religious nationalists, and ultra-Orthodox factions.

item.title: [Euractiv] Roswall: ‘Simplification is not about lowering ambition’
item.description: Environment commissioner accepts petition from activists who fear bonfire of EU nature protection law

item.title: [EU Observer] Moscow elites pleased with US envoy Witkoff and far from agreeing to peace (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,702)
item.description: Starshield, the defense version of Starlink, seems to remain slow despite US assurances that it was fully back. And journalists from Russia reveal what is being discussed by Kremlin and US officials as they seek a deal on Ukraine.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
item.description: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

item.title: [EU Observer] New EU-wide asylum law ends up in court in Italy
item.description: An Egyptian national who sought protection in Italy after arriving on the island of Lampedusa in August may end up dealing a constitutional blow to the EU's asylum laws after seeking legal counsel.

item.title: [Euractiv] Meta delays AI business terms amid media sector outcry
item.description: Tech giant is facing regulatory scrutiny after backlash from press publishers

item.title: [EU Observer] Jewish groups clash over whether EU antisemitism envoy should influence Israel policy, as controversial von Schnurbein goes back to Berlin
item.description: Katharina von Schnurbein caused controversy in May 2025 when she briefed EU ambassadors in Tel Aviv that proposed EU trade sanctions on Israel were based on "rumours about Jews, as opposed to facts".

item.title: [Euractiv] INTERVIEW: High energy costs hamper EU pharma independence
item.description: The EU is one of the few regions worldwide that does not offer industries lower electricity prices for bulk purchases

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ukraine and Russia each exchange 270 prisoners of war
item.description: Kyiv thanked the United States and the United Arab Emirates for facilitating the third stage of the swap.

item.title: [EU Observer] Big fish hooked in Hungary, as Orbán’s ex-bank chief placed in custody (Day 163 of the Tisza government)
item.description: Prosecutors are circling Orbán’s ex‑bank chief, as Magyar rewrites Hungary’s budget.

item.title: [Euractiv] Romania blames Russia for new deadly attack on ship
item.description: Romanian authorities said there were 10 Ukrainian and three Azerbaijani crew on board

item.title: [Euractiv] Spanish parties reveal candidates lists ahead of elections
item.description: Political parties shuffle its leadership ahead of the elections

item.title: [Politico Europe] French prosecutors open hate crime probe after deadly drive-by shooting
item.description: The incident, which killed at least one person, is being treated as a possible act of terror.

item.title: [DW] Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament
item.description: After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU prosecutor probes EPP over consultant contracts
item.description: The European Parliament refused to refund some of the conservative party's pre-election spending.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Drone hits another ship in Black Sea near Romania, killing at least 1 sailor
item.description: President Nicușor Dan said the incident was part of Russia’s “escalation” of the war in Ukraine.

item.title: [EU Observer] Putting the clocks back this Sunday – yet millions of Europeans don’t want to
item.description: On Sunday, Europeans will once again turn their clocks back by one hour. The familiar ritual will again raise the same question: did the European Union not decide years ago to end seasonal clock changes?

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘If stress in France ends up contaminating the rest of the eurozone, the ECB will have to do something,’ says French economist
item.description: France needs spending cuts, but its politics can’t deliver them. Former Macron adviser and economist Shahin Vallée on the protests, Le Pen and Mélenchon’s debt plans, and the dilemma holding back ECB intervention.

item.title: [EU Observer] [EXCLUSIVE] Leaked WhatsApps between ex-EU commissioner Reynders and senior Belgian spy reveal attempts to bury allegations of his possible Russia ties
item.description: The messages, seen by EUobserver and published here in full, now form evidence in a Belgian police investigation into Reynders on money-laundering charges, which paints them in a potentially criminal light.

item.title: [EU Observer] The EU media connects Europe’s connectors – allow us to help
item.description: Outlets such as EUobserver do more than report on European affairs. They provide a space where different perspectives meet, complex policy debates become accessible and stakeholders can better understand the choices shaping the continent.
